title: The 4 Best Fitness Trackers Under $50
metaDescription: Our 4 picks for fitness trackers under $50, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at fitness trackers under $50 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Amazfit Band 7
products.blurb: Key specs: 18-day battery life, 1.47-inch AMOLED display, 120 sports modes.
strengths: 18-day battery life beats every tracker in this category regardless of price
AMOLED display and 120 sports modes are unusually generous specs for the price
No subscription needed for full sleep, heart rate, and activity history
Alexa built-in adds smart assistant functionality most budget bands skip entirely
limitations: Connected GPS only, no built-in chip for phone-free route tracking
Zepp companion app is functional but less refined than Fitbit or Garmin Connect
Band material and clasp show wear faster than pricier alternatives over many months

products.name: Samsung Galaxy Fit3
products.blurb: Key specs: 1.6-inch AMOLED display, 13-day battery life, 100+ workout modes.
strengths: 1.6-inch display is the largest and sharpest in this price bracket
13-day battery life comfortably covers two weeks of regular use
100+ workout modes cover more niche activities than most budget bands bother with
Tight integration with Samsung Health for Galaxy phone owners
limitations: Requires an Android phone for full functionality, no iPhone support
No built-in GPS, relies entirely on a connected phone
Fewer third-party app integrations than Fitbit or Garmin's ecosystems

products.name: Garmin vivofit 4 Activity Tracker
strengths: 1+ year battery life with no charging
Simple step, sleep and activity tracking

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
